description: A dependency here merges itself as soon as CI is green, so without a wait the only review a new release gets is that it compiled, and CI cannot tell a benign release from a compromised or withdrawn one. Three days is roughly how long that takes to surface. The wait sits at the top level rather than on a rule because a rule covers the managers somebody listed, and the first one here listed gomod and npm: that left every GitHub Action, the builder image and the four tool versions the workflows pin inline free to merge themselves on the day they were published, four of those actions being the ones that run in the jobs that push and sign the release image, which the checks exercise with push disabled and never sign with. Nothing merges itself inside those three days, and with internalChecksFilter left at its default of strict nothing is opened either: the update is listed on the Dependency Dashboard under Pending Status Checks until it has aged. Set internalChecksFilter to flexible if the pull request is wanted immediately with only the automerge held back. Where the platform raises a vulnerability alert the fix for it is not held back, since vulnerabilityAlerts sets minimumReleaseAge to null by default and nothing here overrides that; alerts are off on this repository today, so nothing takes that path yet.

packageRules.description: Actions are pinned to commit digests (helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests). Renovate bumps the digest and rewrites the trailing '# vX.Y.Z' comment, so pinning stays maintainable rather than rotting.

The builder image is pinned by digest as well as by tag, for the reason the actions are. Scoped to the Dockerfile so the throwaway database in compose.yaml, which nothing ships, is left as a readable tag.

The builder image and the GO_VERSION the jobs test with are one toolchain, and a test fails if the two files name different ones, so they have to move in a single pull request. Both resolve to depName 'golang': the image through the dockerfile manager, GO_VERSION through the customManager below.

The floor in go.mod is the third name for that same toolchain, and Renovate leaves the `go` directive alone unless asked to, so the floor is whatever an automerged dependency bump last raised it to: an x/crypto update left it at 1.26.0, a release line below the image and unpatched since the day it shipped. A build from source compiles with whatever local Go clears that floor, so `go run ./cmd/soiree` ran on a toolchain no job here tests, and govulncheck read 26 standard-library vulnerabilities off it while the same scanner on the shipped toolchain read none. It joins the group above so the three move in one pull request: a floor above the pinned builder is what the test in cmd/soiree fails on, and a patch release the builder image or setup-go has not caught up with turns the checks red rather than merging itself, since every automerge here waits for green.

customManagers.description: Keep GO_VERSION in the workflows in step with the Dockerfile, so CI tests the same toolchain the image ships.

The CI tools that are installed by version rather than by action digest. Pinning them is what the workflow file asks for; without a manager each pin then rots, which is the same problem wearing the other face.
golangci-lint, whose version is an input to the action rather than part of its digest. The trailing comment on that line names the package and is what this matches on.
govulncheck, which CI runs straight from its module path.
